work.title: The Building Record
work.alt: Interior of Muchacho Decatur, a Freeman project
work.description: A building told through its drawings, photographs, details and people. The Muchacho record is a study, not an approved record.

work.title: Built for Generations
work.description: A documentary series about the people and places behind the work. One pilot proposed; no production commissioned.

work.title: Freeman as a publishing house
work.description: One coherent catalogue for projects, photographs, records, films, and collaborations.

notes.subject: THE BIGGER IDEA
notes.title: A builder that publishes.
notes.body: What if Freeman becomes known not only for the buildings we deliver, but for the attention we pay to them? The record is evidence of care, not just promotion.
notes.aside: A working hypothesis, not a strategy approved by the company.

notes.subject: BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT
notes.title: Make the work open doors.
notes.body: A beautiful record of a project should travel to the architect, the owner, the operator, and the next person thinking about building something remarkable.
notes.aside: The commercial purpose behind the creative work.

notes.subject: PROCESS
notes.title: An hour every week.
notes.body: I want this place to change as the real work changes. Not a monthly spectacle. A steady record of what we did, saw, made, and learned.
notes.aside: The rhythm I want for this studio.

questions.title: Which building becomes the first complete Record?
questions.desc: Muchacho is the working study; original drawings and permission are not yet in hand.

questions.title: Should I explore one pilot with Tristan?
questions.desc: A conversation is the first step. No quote, agreement, or shoot exists.

questions.title: How should Freeman sign the publishing work?
questions.desc: The globe is a study. The eagle is an existing production mark.
